title: Wine Wimsey Review · Oct 26
subtitle: 12 feed (10 images + 2 TOBIs at #4 and #8) and 4 stories, for posting Mon Oct 26 · 3 inbox quotes now (#1 cabin, #3 lost things, #10 swearing; the rest written fresh and checked against the used list) · Characters: 5 The Hot Mess and 5 The Homebody on the feed (stories split 2 and 2) · 2 new TOBIs under 130 characters · Caption mix: 4 short, 6 See More · Flag: #6 (shower) shows her bare shoulders behind frosted glass, easy to redo if you want her covered · Redo round: #2, #4 and #7 now have wine instead of tea, both TOBIs rewritten

posts.quote: I’m not saying menopause has made me feral. I’m just saying that moving to a cabin in the woods and becoming the lady the locals warn their kids about sounds more reasonable every day.
posts.caption: I've picked out the cabin. It has a porch, a rocking chair, and a view of absolutely nothing, which is my favorite view. There would be a lantern, a good stack of firewood and a reputation. Kids would dare each other to knock. I'd wave from the rocker, very slowly. It all feels peaceful when I picture it. Right now I'm just planning the garden, and the sign I'd hang that says nothing at all.
posts.first: My husband says if I go, he's coming too, as long as the cabin has a decent signal. I told him the whole point is that it doesn't. He's thinking it over. I'm giving him until spring.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with wild pink curls in a rocking chair on the porch of a tiny cabin in the woods at dusk, holding a glass of red wine and a lantern with a mischievous grin, two tiny child silhouettes pointing from the edge of the trees. Text at the top reads: I’m not saying menopause has made me feral. I’m just saying that moving to a cabin in the woods and becoming the lady the locals warn their kids about sounds more reasonable every day.

posts.quote: My idea of a wild Saturday night is a new puzzle, a fresh pot of tea, and nobody calling.
posts.caption: Last Saturday I opened a thousand-piece puzzle of a lighthouse and did not look up until the edges were done and my glass had been refilled twice. The phone stayed face down. The house was quiet in the good way, the kind where you can hear the clock and feel fine about it. By eleven I'd found the whole sky. I went to bed proud, with a very specific kind of satisfaction that only comes from a corner piece clicking into place.
posts.first: I keep the box lid propped on the sideboard so I can see where I'm headed. My neighbor says it's the most dangerous hobby she's ever heard of, because you can't stop at one piece. She's right. I'm on the lighthouse's roof now.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a delighted woman with pink curls sitting at a coffee table with a half-finished jigsaw puzzle, a bottle of red wine and a glass of red wine, and a glowing lamp. Text at the top reads: My idea of a wild Saturday night is a new puzzle, a fresh pot of tea, and nobody calling.

posts.quote: Menopause has been amazingly good at helping me lose things. My keys, my patience, my words... But not one single damn pound has gone anywhere.
posts.caption: The keys were in the fridge. The patience, I think, is in the car. The pounds are right where I left them.
posts.first: Last week I found my phone in the freezer next to the peas. I wasn't even upset. I just said 'well, that's where it lives now,' and went to find my glasses, which were on my head.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of an exasperated woman with a messy bun searching her pockets and lifting couch cushions in a living room, a glass of red wine on the side table and a smug bathroom scale in the corner. Text at the top reads: Menopause has been amazingly good at helping me lose things. My keys, my patience, my words... But not one single damn pound has gone anywhere.

posts.quote: I used to plan for the future. Now I plan for the next time I can sit down.
posts.first: Last week at the grocery store I spotted a bench near the bread aisle and mapped my whole trip around it. It was the best part of the day and I regret nothing.

posts.quote: Nothing says self-care like clean sheets, warm socks, and a firm decision not to answer the phone.
posts.caption: Sunday is sheet day in this house. Fresh from the dryer, tucked in tight, the pillow turned to the cool side. By seven I was in bed with my thickest socks and a glass of something red. The phone buzzed twice and I let it. It's amazing how little in life can't wait until morning. If it's urgent, they'll call back, and if they don't, it wasn't. I slept like I was twelve.
posts.first: My daughter says I'm hard to reach on Sunday nights. I told her that's by design, and also that I love her. She said the second part was a nice touch. She was right. It was.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a blissful woman with pink curls snuggled in a freshly made bed with crisp white sheets, thick fuzzy socks poking out, holding a glass of red wine, a phone face down on the nightstand. Text at the top reads: Nothing says self-care like clean sheets, warm socks, and a firm decision not to answer the phone.

posts.quote: My phone says storage is almost full. I’d delete something, but I’m emotionally attached to 400 screenshots of recipes I’ll never make.
posts.caption: The lasagna with seven cheeses is in there. So is the pasta that looks like a flower. I'm keeping both.
posts.first: I tried deleting photos once and got as far as one blurry picture of my thumb. Then I got nervous and closed the app. We're at 98 percent now, and I've chosen peace.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a guilty woman on a couch clutching her phone protectively to her chest, the screen showing only a red exclamation mark. Text at the top reads: My phone says storage is almost full. I’d delete something, but I’m emotionally attached to 400 screenshots of recipes I’ll never make.

posts.quote: I do my best thinking in the shower. Too bad I forget every brilliant idea the second I turn the water off.
posts.caption: Yesterday I figured out the whole week. Meals, errands, a plan for the closet, even what to say to my brother-in-law. It was a masterpiece, all of it, delivered somewhere between the shampoo and the conditioner. Then I reached for the towel and it was gone, like a dream. I stood there dripping, trying to find even one piece. All I came up with was that I need more conditioner. That one stuck, naturally.
posts.first: I've started keeping a pencil and a notepad near the bathroom door. So far I've written down a single word, and it's 'hair.' I'm still trying to figure out what I meant by it. I'm sure it was important.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wide-eyed woman with a lathered messy bun behind a frosted glass shower door with steam, a glowing lightbulb above her head and a fading thought bubble. Text at the top reads: I do my best thinking in the shower. Too bad I forget every brilliant idea the second I turn the water off.

posts.quote: Every year my bucket list gets shorter and my “do not disturb” list gets longer.
posts.first: This year's bucket list is one item: a quiet afternoon with the phone off. I'm halfway through crossing it off as I write this. It's going very well.

posts.quote: My dream day has no meetings, no errands, and nobody saying my name in that tone.
posts.caption: You know the tone. It starts soft, goes up at the end, and means something is about to be asked of you. I heard it all through the years, from kids, bosses, and one very persistent dog groomer. Now my favorite sound is a quiet porch in the afternoon with the leaves coming down. I read two chapters, finished my glass, and nobody needed a thing. It was the closest I've come to a miracle this year.
posts.first: I told my husband the plan for Saturday is to be unavailable. He asked for how long. I said I'd let him know. He's been very supportive, mostly because he's got plans of his own with the garage and a radio.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a peaceful woman with pink curls reclined in a porch chair with a book in her lap, a soft blanket and a glass of red wine, eyes closed in golden autumn light. Text at the top reads: My dream day has no meetings, no errands, and nobody saying my name in that tone.

posts.quote: I like my coffee like my mornings: slow, strong, and not to be spoken to.
posts.caption: Don't ask me anything before the second cup. I'll answer, and then we'll both regret it.
posts.first: My husband learned this after twenty years of marriage and one memorable misunderstanding about the dishwasher. Now he just slides a mug across the counter and backs away slowly. It's the closest thing we have to a love language.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a half-asleep woman at a kitchen counter cradling an enormous steaming mug with both hands and a flat unwelcoming expression. Text at the top reads: I like my coffee like my mornings: slow, strong, and not to be spoken to.

posts.quote: Fall is just nature’s way of saying it’s time to wear a sweater and cancel plans.
posts.caption: The leaves agree with me. Nobody has ever regretted a night in.
posts.first: I had a dinner invitation for Friday and a fuzzy sweater in the drawer. We both had to make choices. I picked the sweater, and I'd like it noted that my decision-making has never been sharper.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a satisfied woman with pink curls in an oversized sweater curled up in a floral armchair holding her phone, with a pumpkin on the side table and an autumn tree outside the window. Text at the top reads: Fall is just nature’s way of saying it’s time to wear a sweater and cancel plans.

posts.quote: I don’t swear because I have a small vocabulary. I just know when “Well, that’s unfortunate” isn’t going to cover this much bullshit.
posts.caption: Saturday I burned the pot, flooded the sink and dropped a full bag of flour in one four-minute window. I stood there. I let out a quiet 'well, that's unfortunate.' My husband looked at me and said I should maybe go outside. He was right, and it's been a very polite weekend since. Some days the plain version just isn't enough, and I've learned to hold my breath, count to ten and then pick a word with a few more letters in it.
posts.first: I keep a tidy list of what I'd say if nobody were listening. It's a short list and it's mostly nouns. I've decided it counts as self-control that I've never read it out loud.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a calm, deadpan woman with a messy bun holding a glass of red wine in a chaotic kitchen with an overflowing sink, a smoking burnt pot and a spilled bag of flour. Text at the top reads: I don’t swear because I have a small vocabulary. I just know when “Well, that’s unfortunate” isn’t going to cover this much bullshit.

stories.quote: Be kind to yourself. You’re doing better than you think and worse than you could. Both are fine.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a gentle smiling woman with a shrug sitting on a park bench among fall leaves holding a thermos. Text at the top reads: Be kind to yourself. You’re doing better than you think and worse than you could. Both are fine.

stories.quote: A quiet evening at home isn’t laziness. It’s my charging station.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a relaxed woman with pink curls in a floral armchair under a lamp with a blanket and a cup of tea, with a green battery icon floating above her head. Text at the top reads: A quiet evening at home isn’t laziness. It’s my charging station.

stories.quote: I don’t have trust issues. I have “I believed the weather app and now I’m soaked” issues.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a soaked woman with a drooping messy bun standing in the rain on a sidewalk glaring at her phone, which shows a sun icon. Text at the top reads: I don’t have trust issues. I have “I believed the weather app and now I’m soaked” issues.

stories.quote: Some of my best friends are the ones who never mind if I show up in my robe.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with pink curls in a fluffy lavender bathrobe laughing on a sofa with a neatly dressed friend holding a teacup, a plate of cookies between them. Text at the top reads: Some of my best friends are the ones who never mind if I show up in my robe.
